articles.title: Disciples review – fresh-faced boys are sucked into a nightmare of extremism in India
articles.summary: A prestigious school in the holy city of Varanasi and its controversial, dogmatic teachings are the subject of this shocking documentary. The effect of political and religious indoctrination on young minds resembles a slow-release poison.
body: The film opens with controversial speeches made by the school’s spiritual leader, Guru Avimuktesh, who advocates the abolition of religious freedom, and for Indian Muslims to either convert to Hinduism or leave for Pakistan. A prominent Hindu figure with a large following, he personally oversees the entrance exam, a sequence captured in dynamic handheld shots. While boys take the test, their parents look on with apprehension and anxiety; to be accepted would be an honour, not only for their child but for the whole family.

For those who do get in to Vidya Mutth, what follows is far from a glorious, enlightening experience. Focusing on two new entrants called Satyarth and Hari, the film documents their daily routines, which largely revolve around Sanskrit classes. The learning of this ancient script, supposedly to maintain a linguistic tradition, is actually in service of religious dogmatism; in between classes, Guru Avimuktesh continues to preach Islamophobic and casteist ideas, packaged as fact.
points: A prestigious school in the holy city of Varanasi and its controversial, dogmatic teachings are the subject of this shocking documentary.
The effect of political and religious indoctrination on young minds resembles a slow-release poison.

articles.title: On Different Grounds review – Cupid’s-conspiracy romcom brings Nollywood and Bollywood together
articles.summary: Mildred Okwo’s earnest film about the conflicting romantic wishes in a Nigerian family struggles to connect with its promising premise. It’s a stretch for this Nigerian romcom to bill itself “the first Nollywood-Bollywood collaboration” based on the fact that it features, in Nimesh Diliprai Desai…
body: Silk-tressed bachelorette Aurora (Abena Akuaba) is being browbeaten by her businessman dad Eyimofe (Bob-Manuel Udokwu) to marry snoozefest suitor Tobore (Ifeanyi Kalu). She is hardly enthused when he parrots his criteria for embarking on “a collaboration with an individual or brand”: “value check, common interest, due diligence and critical analysis.” (Tobore ticks the boxes.) But she agrees to set a date on one condition: that Eyimofe must invite her mother, Isioma (Jennifer Eliogu) – booted out by Eyimofe many years back for wanting to pursue her career – to the big day.

Aurora’s plan to rekindle romance in her uptight executive dad is a sly, fun starting point – made even more urgent when success on that front becomes critical to the future of her secret childhood crush on Rajesh (Raina), a pristine-bouffanted dreamboat. But this Cupid’s conspiracy, which might have made a fine 1940s screwball, nosedives in Okwo’s hands, as she sandwiches agonisingly leaden farce (such as the cough Aurora suddenly develops in Rajesh’s presence) between slabs of family melodrama.

articles.title: Mark Ruffalo fires back at Paramount Skydance after it accuses him of using ‘antisemitic tropes’
articles.summary: Actor says highlighting role of Oracle CEO Larry Ellison in media company’s merger with Warner Bros Discovery has been ‘dishonestly framed as being anti-Israel’ Mark Ruffalo has fired back at Paramount Skydance after the media company accused him of invoking “antisemitic tropes” in his criticism of…
body: The actor, who has long been outspoken against Israel’s military conduct in Gaza and for the rights of Palestinians, shared a statement on social media on Friday in which he highlighted the links between Paramount Skydance, run by CEO David Ellison, and Oracle, the technology company run by Ellison’s father, Larry.

Oracle has supplied software to the Israel Defense Forces, ministry of defense, air force, government and police for decades. Shmulik Hauser, head of Oracle’s sales division, told Ynet last year: “Supporting Israel is in our DNA – even if it costs us clients. That’s our agenda.”

On Friday Ruffalo shared a video of Oracle executive vice-chair, Safra Catz, describing the “really profoundly scary technology” it provided to Israel after the 7 October attack by Hamas in 2023. Above the video, Ruffalo took aim at Larry Ellison, who he accused of “using [Oracle] to fund his son David’s Warner Bros acquisition”.
Larry Ellison, who is worth an estimated $189bn, agreed to personally backstop $40.4bn in equity financing to help Paramount Skydance acquire WBD in a $110.9bn deal.

articles.title: Deauville American Film Festival Reveals Industry Lineup
articles.summary: The Deauville American Film Festival has revealed the lineup for the industry section of its 2026 edition. The Deauville Industry Days sidebar, taking place over two days at the festival being held at the French seaside town, will incorporate various talks, panels and sessions.
body: Focusing on on-screen talent, the panel ‘How to Break in the U.S. as a French Actor, will see casting director Mathilde Snodgrass, actress Mathilde Ollivier (“Overlord”) and talent agent Raphaelle Danglard discuss how to make waves in Hollywood.

Elsewhere, CNC’s Joanna Verner and Celine Leclercq will take part in ‘The Financing Schemes in France’ panel, about tax rebate opportunities for international productions. Rounding out the industry section, the ‘A U.S. Production Shot in France’ session will explore how Netflix’s U.S. rom-com “Champagne Problems,” from Mark Steven Johnson and starring Minka Kelly and Tom Wozniczka, was filmed in France in 2024 with producers David Atrakchi and Boris Mendza.

The Deauville American Film Festival has already unveiled a buzzy lineup of films screening this year, alongside a heavy assortment of stars set to receive honors. Among those getting awards are Brendan Fraser, Ethan Hawke, Faye Dunaway, Susan Sarandon, Sophie Thatcher and Patrick Schwarzenegger.

articles.title: ‘Game of Thrones’ Star Kristofer Hivju Turns to Rom-Com With ‘True Love’ by ‘Little Did I Know’s’ Martina Haag (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Norwegian star actor Kristofer Hivju (“Game of Thrones,” “Red One”, “Beck”) will play opposite Frida Hallgren (from Oscar-nominated “As It Is in Heaven”) in the upcoming Swedish-Croatian rom-com “True Love” (working title).
body: As with ‘ Little Did I know,” “True Love”’s starting point is deceit and divorce and how to bounce back when you’re over 50.
According to the logline, when Ellinor (played by Hallgren) is dumped by her husband after 20 years of marriage, she loses faith in life.

When she wins €40 million ($46 million) immediately after, she finds it even harder to trust anyone. But then she meets Henrik (Hivju). The latter grew up at the elite Lundsberg boarding school, where his mother worked as a cleaner. To fit in, he learned to lie, and became an irresistibly charming master of deception. Their relationship should never work, but what if they’re exactly what the other needs? “As both main characters are flawed and a bit extreme in the beginning of the film, it was important for us to find great actors that are warm and relatable: Real people in exaggerated situations, that we want to be with and see get better,” said Hivju and Hallgren Haag.

articles.title: ‘I Plant My Hand in the Garden’ Blurs the Line Between Autobiography and Fiction to Explore Identity and Family (Exclusive Venice Trailer)
articles.summary: Hoda Taheri and Boris Hadžija's feature debut, premiering in the Venice Days competition, asks "how institutions, such as marriage, nationality and gender, assign roles that feel both real and constructed."
body: Hoda and Boris are in love and are expecting a child. So, they decide to marry and officially form a family together. But as the wedding draws nearer, it starts to dawn on them that becoming a family may require them to reinvent what it means to be a couple.

“Together, they decide to marry and raise the child, imagining a future built on their own terms,” reads a synopsis for I Plant My Hand in the Garden. “As they prepare for the wedding and enter more deeply into each other’s worlds, their relationship is unsettled by bureaucracy, family expectations and histories neither of them can leave behind. Surrounded by relatives, memories and inherited ideas of love and parenthood, Hoda and Boris begin to question the roles they are about to take on. What starts as a plan to become a family gradually opens into a more intimate and uncertain question: can they reinvent what it means to be a couple without losing what brought them together?”

Taheri and Hadžija star in the movie, along with Branka Hadžija, Jahandokht Taheri and Hadi Khanjanpour. The cinematography comes courtesy of Lithuanian camera wiz Vytautas Katkus. Boris Hadžija also handled editing.

articles.title: Busan Film Festival Sets 23 Titles for Vision Korea, Vision Asia Sections
articles.summary: Busan has selected 12 Korean indies and 11 films from emerging directors from across Asia for its 2026 edition, with the main competition lineup still to come.
body: The Busan International Film Festival has unveiled 23 features for its Vision Korea and Vision Asia sections, filling out its showcase for Korean and Asian independent cinema ahead of the reveal of this year’s main competition slate.

BIFF earlier named Kim Jong-kwan’s The Table: Day and Night as its 2026 opening film. The Seoul cafe-set romance, a loose follow-up to his 2016 feature The Table, will world premiere at the Busan Cinema Center on Oct. 6, with star Kim Minha hosting the opening ceremony. Michelle Yeoh will receive the Asian Filmmaker of the Year honor, Hong Kong auteur Ann Hui the Chanel-backed Camellia Award and festival founder Kim Dong-ho the Korean Cinema Award.
The festival’s full competition lineup is still to come. BIFF will unveil its complete official selection in Seoul on Sept. 1 at its official opening press conference.
The 31st Busan International Film Festival runs Oct. 6-15, with the Asian Contents & Film Market held Oct. 10-13.

articles.title: 25 Years Ago Today: A John Carpenter Flop Opened—And He Didn't Direct Again For Nine Years
articles.summary: John Carpenter is one of the greatest directors to ever do it, but after this sci-fi horror flick flopped, everything changed.
body: John Carpenter hasn't directed a movie in 16 years. That's a real shame, because the Horror Master gave us some all-time classics such as "Halloween" and "The Thing," among many others. But at least part of the reason he walked away from directing movies has to do with a colossal flop he directed, starring Jason Statham, titled "Ghosts of Mars." Released 25 years ago today, it was the beginning of the end for Carpenter's career as a director of feature films.

The movie takes place in the future, where hundreds of thousands of people now live and work across Mars, mining the planet for its abundant natural resources. One of these mining operations uncovers a deadly secret: a long-dormant Martian civilization whose warriors are taking over human bodies. A rag-tag group of soldiers and prisoners must band together to stop them. Natasha Henstridge ("Species"), Pam Grier ("Jackie Brown"), and Ice Cube ("Friday") also star.
points: John Carpenter is one of the greatest directors to ever do it, but after this sci-fi horror flick flopped, everything changed.

articles.title: Lanterns Episode 2 Gives Us A Better Version Of An Infamous Marvel Flop
articles.summary: The second episode of HBO's Lanterns TV series gives audiences a much better version of what Marvel tried to do with the disastrous Secret Invasion.
body: Are you afraid... of spoilers? This article discusses major plot details from "Lanterns" Episode 2.

The "Lanterns" series premiere seems to have gone over well with viewers, even with the ending twist that sends shockwaves throughout the rest of the DC Universe, but it's clear that there's more to this story than what first meets the eye. As Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) investigate the mysterious shooting in Rushville, Nebraska, the final moments make it clear that Hal was right all along. This supposedly "terrestrial" event involves aliens, and now it's up to Earth's first Green Lantern and his trainee to figure out what to do next.

Ringing any bells? If this reminds you of Marvel's "Secret Invasion," well, you're not alone. The notorious flop may not be the most flattering comparison, but DC is already succeeding where its rival failed.
points: The second episode of HBO's Lanterns TV series gives audiences a much better version of what Marvel tried to do with the disastrous Secret Invasion.
